primitives.note: Bravado arms Taric's next two basic attacks (within a 5s window, refreshed and re-granted by subsequent ability casts, capped at two stored attacks) with 100% total attack speed and bonus magic damage; this is the primary attack-side damage source in the fight.
Bonus armor is converted into magic damage: 15% bonus armor on each Bravado-empowered attack, 50% bonus armor on Dazzle. Armor bought/gained during the fight directly scales both damage sources.

Every ability cast (Q/W/E/R) triggers Bravado, which reduces the *remaining* cooldowns of Taric's other basic abilities via an ability-haste-based formula. In the damage fight this mainly matters for how often Dazzle (E) can be recast.
Dazzle deals a single instance of magic damage to the dummy after a fixed 1s wind-up, then goes on cooldown; recast on cooldown for the whole fight.
W's passive grants Taric bonus armor (6-10% of his own armor) while self-bound; this raises the bonus-armor pool that feeds P's and E's stat-conversion damage.

Mana costs (60/60/40/100) and E's cooldown limit how many Bravado-triggering casts Taric can fit into the 15s window; whether Q can be spammed at 0 charges purely to proc Bravado changes the achievable cast cadence substantially.

needsBespoke.why: Two things fall outside a simple primitive: (1) Bravado's empowered-attack queue is stateful in a way generic 'empowered-attack' doesn't capture — it stores up to two charges, the first landed attack refreshes the 5s timer, and a subsequent ability cast both refreshes the timer AND grants a second stored charge only if exactly one remains; this queue must be tracked explicitly against attack timing. (2) The cooldown reduction from Bravado is not a flat number but a saturating ability-haste curve (1 + Haste/(Haste+100)) applied to *remaining* cooldown, and the bin itself marks the underlying calculation piece ('CooldownMultiplierCalculationPart') as unresolved — this needs bespoke logic rather than a static cooldown-manipulation value.
